title: Oft in Sorrow, Oft in Woe
description: Oft in Sorrow, Oft in Woe in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Kirke White wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 500.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Oft in sor-row, oft in woe, On-ward, Christ-ians, on-ward go! Bear the toil, main-tain the strife, Strength-ened with the Bread of Life.

lines: Oft in sorrow, oft in woe,
Bear the toil, maintain the strife,
Strengthened with the Bread of Life.
Let not sorrow dim your eye;
Soon shall every tear be dry.
Let not woe your course impede;
Great your help if great your need.
Let your drooping hearts be glad;
Fight, nor think the battle long;
Victory soon shall tune your song.
More than conquerors you shall prove;
Though begirt with many a foe,

licence: Public domain: Henry Kirke White died in 1806.
credits: Words by Henry Kirke White (1785–1806), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
